MLX vs Ollama on Mac (2026): Which Runtime Is Fastest?

answer_raw:
MLX is faster for pure inference benchmarks, but Ollama is the practical choice for agentic workflows.

**MLX** is the performance leader; on an M4 Max, it can run a 35B model roughly twice as fast as Ollama, hitting around 60-70+ tok/s compared to Ollama's ~35 tok/s [4]. However, the comparison is often about use case rather than raw speed: **Ollama** is the standard for developer-facing agents and workflows, whereas **MLX** is primarily utilized for heavy-duty benchmarks and model validation [1]. It is worth noting that as of March 2026, Ollama (v0.19+) rebuilt its Mac engine to run on top of MLX, meaning the performance gap between the two has narrowed significantly as the "easy-mode" runtime adopted the faster framework [8].

Regarding your capacity, the biggest model you can realistically run is a **70B** model using **Q4 quantization** [3].

With 48GB of unified memory, you can run **30B** models at full precision or load **70B** models at a 4-bit quantization level [3]. At the 70B tier, the hardware limitations of the M4 Pro become apparent: due to the 273 GB/s memory bandwidth, you can expect a ceiling of roughly 6 tokens/sec, though real-world throughput typically reaches about **14 tok/s** [7]. If you need significantly faster generation for 70B models, you would need to move to an M4 Max/Studio tier to access higher bandwidth [7].
